title: Name/secure License+PII reviewer and domain (oncology) reviewer (blocking gate roles)
context: Ewing sarcoma corpus work touches per-article licensing and potential case-report/PII content, so two blocking reviewer roles must be filled before any per-article curation or extraction proceeds: a License+PII reviewer and a domain (oncology) reviewer. Binding cancer guardrails apply: open-access (PMC OA Subset) / aggregate / de-identified data only; no identifiable patient data; no medical advice; provenance on every assertion. This task names/secures those reviewers; it is a hard gate for pilot-007 and every medium-risk extraction task (no self-review).
objective: Identify and secure a named License+PII reviewer and a named domain (oncology) reviewer, documenting their roles as blocking gate reviewers.
acceptanceCriteria: A named License+PII reviewer is recorded (affiliation + contact channel) with scope: license-bucket decisions and PII/case-report dispositions sign-off.
A named domain (oncology) reviewer is recorded with scope: scientific-faithfulness sign-off on extracted assertions.
Both roles are documented as blocking gates: pilot-007 and all medium-risk extraction tasks cannot be marked delivered without the relevant reviewer sign-off, and no author reviews their own work.
If a role cannot be filled, the blocker is surfaced explicitly and dependent tasks remain blocked.
